text: When Mordecai learned all that had happened, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the middle of the city crying loudly and bitterly.
He went only as far as the king's gate, since no one was allowed to enter the king's gate dressed in sackcloth.
In every province the king's command and decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

When Esther's female attendants and eunuchs came and told her about Mordecai, the queen was overcome with distress. She sent clothing for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth, but he would not accept it.
Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs assigned to attend her, and ordered him to find out from Mordecai what was happening and why.
So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate,
and Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of silver Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury for the destruction of the Jews.

He also gave Hathach a copy of the written decree issued in Susa ordering their destruction, so that he could show it to Esther, explain it to her, and urge her to go before the king to beg for mercy and plead for her people.
Hathach went back and reported Mordecai's words to Esther.
Then Esther spoke to Hathach and sent him back to Mordecai with this reply:

All the king's officials and the people of his provinces know that if any man or woman approaches the king in the inner courtyard without being summoned, the law is the same for everyone — death, unless the king holds out his gold scepter to spare that person's life. And I have not been summoned to appear before the king for the last thirty days.
When Esther's words were relayed to Mordecai,
he sent back this answer: Do not imagine that because you are in the king's palace you alone will escape the fate of all the Jews.

For if you remain silent at this time, relief and rescue for the Jews will rise from another place, but you and your father's family will be destroyed. And who knows whether you have come to your royal position for a time like this?
Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:

Go and gather all the Jews who are in Susa, and fast on my behalf. Do not eat or drink anything for three days, night or day. My attendants and I will fast in the same way. After that, I will go in to the king, even though it is against the law, and if I perish, I perish.
So Mordecai went away and did everything just as Esther had instructed him.
